Extended and unscented Kalman filters

Source: R/nonlinear.R
ctrl_ekf.Rd

Nonlinear state estimation for a discrete time ctrl_nlsys with additive noise, \(x_{k+1} = f(k, x_k, u_k) + w_k\), \(y_k = h(k, x_k, u_k) + v_k\), using the conventions of ctrl_kalman_filter() (x0, P0 are the prior at the first sample; each step updates with \(y_k\) and then predicts; rows of y that are entirely NA skip the update). Row k of the data is passed to f and h as the sample index k - 1, the 0-based convention of ctrl_nl_simulate().

Usage

ctrl_ekf(
  sys,
  y,
  u = NULL,
  Qn,
  Rn,
  x0 = NULL,
  P0 = NULL,
  covariances = c("all", "variances", "final")
)

ctrl_ukf(
  sys,
  y,
  u = NULL,
  Qn,
  Rn,
  x0 = NULL,
  P0 = NULL,
  alpha = 1,
  beta = 2,
  kappa = 0,
  covariances = c("all", "variances", "final")
)

Arguments

sys

Discrete time ctrl_nlsys.

y

Measurements (T x p).

u

Inputs (T x m) or NULL.

Qn, Rn

Process and measurement noise covariances.

x0, P0

Prior mean and covariance.

covariances

"all" (default), "variances" or "final"; see ctrl_kalman_filter().

alpha, beta, kappa

Unscented transform parameters.

Value

A list of class c("ctrl_nl_filter", "ctrl_kalman_filter") with filtered, variances, P_filtered (NULL with covariances = "variances" or "final"; variances is NULL with "final"), P_final, innovations, nis and loglik. It has no predicted covariances, so ctrl_kalman_smoother() does not accept it.

Details

  • ctrl_ekf() linearizes f and h at the current estimate with central finite differences (or the model's analytic jacobian) and uses the Joseph-form covariance update.

  • ctrl_ukf() propagates \(2n + 1\) sigma points (scaled unscented transform with parameters alpha, beta, kappa); it needs no Jacobians and is exact for linear models.

Both are approximations for nonlinear models: their covariances are not guaranteed to be consistent, and they can diverge for strong nonlinearities or poor initialization. Check the normalized innovation squared (nis), whose mean should be close to the number of outputs.

Examples

f <- function(k, x, u, p) c(x[1] + 0.1 * x[2], x[2] - 0.1 * sin(x[1]))
h <- function(k, x, u, p) x[1]
sys <- ctrl_nlsys(f, h, nstates = 2, ninputs = 0, dt = 0.1)
set.seed(1)
x <- c(1, 0)
y <- numeric(100)
for (k in 1:100) {
  y[k] <- x[1] + rnorm(1, sd = 0.05)
  x <- f(k, x, NULL, NULL) + rnorm(2, sd = 0.001)
}
ekf <- ctrl_ekf(sys, y, Qn = 1e-6, Rn = 0.0025, x0 = c(0.8, 0))
ukf <- ctrl_ukf(sys, y, Qn = 1e-6, Rn = 0.0025, x0 = c(0.8, 0))
tail(cbind(ekf$filtered, ukf$filtered), 2)
#>               x1         x2        x1         x2
#>  [99,] -1.276753 -0.7291844 -1.276617 -0.7291842
#> [100,] -1.348630 -0.6332541 -1.348497 -0.6332617
